Hi Sanjay,

Thanks for sending over Lyra's questionnaire. Attached are two artifacts that should address most of the items your procurement and security teams asked about: a concise FAQ and a detailed retention matrix per artifact type. High level answers below for your packet: 

- Data residency: Lyra can select the serving region for hosted API requests at the project level (US-only or EU-only). For US-hosted projects we provision inference instances in a single AWS region you choose (e.g., us-west-2). We do not replicate user request payloads across regions for Lyra projects unless you explicitly enable cross-region backups.

- Data retention: By default, request payloads and model outputs are stored transiently for up to 30 days for troubleshooting and auditability; you can opt into a 24-hour retention policy for your account. The retention matrix in the spreadsheet lists TTLs for: request logs, KV cache checkpoints, debug traces, aggregated metrics, and backups.

- Deletion & purge: We support both API-driven and console-initiated deletion. Deleting data triggers a soft-delete immediately (removed from active indices) and a background purge job that permanently removes backups and replicas within 14 days by default; expedited purge (3 days) is available under an SLA addendum. For critical exports we provide an on-demand export endpoint and will coordinate a secure transfer to your S3 if needed.

- Backups & snapshots: Automated snapshots for stateful serving components are retained for 7 days in the default config; snapshot replication is disabled for tenants pinned to a single region. Manual snapshot retention can be extended if required.

- Access & encryption: All data at rest is encrypted using KMS-managed keys; you can provide a customer-managed key (CMK) per account. Transit uses TLS 1.2+. Audit logs for administrative actions are retained for 90 days in the console by default.

- Compliance: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II certified; we will sign a BAA for covered PHI use cases. The attached FAQ lists the standard certificates and our evidence locations.

I attached the two files and included a short retention matrix so procurement has numbers to pass to finance. If you want, I can loop in Grace for the finer technical details around backups and purge behavior.

Next steps: let me know if your team wants 24-hour retention enabled for your test tenant or if you want a short call to walk through the matrix.

Best,

Hi Sanjay —

Looping in with the technical specifics so procurement and security have precise language for the SOW. Short answers first, followed by an exact phrasing you can paste into a document.

Short answers:
- "Training prompts" / prompt engineering inputs: treated as customer request data. By default they are retained under request logs TTL (30 days), unless your account opts into a 24-hour retention policy. We do not use customer prompts to update model weights.

- Purge scope: our purge job deletes request logs, KV cache checkpoints, associated debug traces, and any incremental snapshots tied to the tenant ID. The purge marks objects for deletion in object storage and deletes indices; object deletion is submitted with versioned object lifecycle rules and garbage collection (typically completes within the purge window).

- Immutable backups: we do not keep indefinite immutable backups for hosted tenants as part of the standard offering. Disaster recovery snapshots are created on schedules you opt into and are stored in the same cloud region under encryption; if you request extended disaster recovery retention we can set up a longer snapshot lifecycle and CMK usage.

- Forensic export & manifest: yes — the API is /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/exports. Exports are signed with a manifest that includes object hashes and timestamps; manifests are retained for 180 days. We'll provide the specific API docs link in the Drive folder.

Suggested SOW language (copy/paste):
"Redwood Inference ("Supplier") will retain customer request data (including developer-provided prompts) for up to 30 days by default. Customer may elect a 24-hour retention policy. Upon deletion request, Supplier will initiate a soft-delete and will permanently purge associated logs, KV cache entries, and region-bound snapshots within 14 days. Expedited purge to 3 days shall be available subject to SLA addendum. Supplier will provide an on-demand export endpoint (/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/exports) that produces a signed manifest. Supplier does not use customer-provided prompts to train or improve model weights for hosted customers unless agreed in writing."

Security notes: all data at rest uses AES-256 with KMS-managed keys; customers may request BYOK (bring-your-own-key). Administrative audit logs (who requested deletion, who approved exports) are retained for 90 days in the console; log exports can be delivered via secure S3.

If you want, Rishi can add a short diagram of how purge flows through object storage lifecycle rules and the timeline for GC.

Thanks —
